verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas documents JavaScript ESM scripts with class syntax as the recommended scripting model, TypeScript scaffolding via create-playcanvas, scripts edited live while the app runs, and local editing through a VS Code extension, so the scripting language is first-class and productive. Nothing in the evidence documents a debugger, and full engine-API exposure from scripts is only implied by the standalone Engine and the 'full engine underneath' wording. Missing for 10: any documented debugger or breakpoint tooling, explicit evidence that scripts expose the complete engine API, and independent hands-on corroboration of scripting productivity.

support.subject: As a game developer, the primary scripting language is productive and fully exposes the engine API, with a debugger behind it

citations.quote: ESM Scripts (`.mjs` files) — Modern ES Module-based scripts using class syntax. Recommended for new projects.

Scripts are the heart of interactivity in PlayCanvas. They're reusable pieces of code that you attach to Entities to define behaviors, handle user input, manage game logic, and bring your projects to life.
With live editing, you can tweak materials, adjust positions, and even modify scripts while your application runs.
Edit its scripts locally with the VS Code extension
Use `create-playcanvas` to scaffold a Vite and TypeScript project for the Engine, React, or Web Components from one of 12 runnable starters.
